releases.title: Voxtral 3 speech models + voice agent API
releases.summary: A new family of speech models plus a voice agent API that chains realtime transcription, a Mistral LLM for reasoning and tool calls, and speech output in one streaming pipeline; it can answer and place calls over SIP and run in browsers and apps over WebRTC. Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 handles 50+ languages with diarization and context biasing ($0.004/min); Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 is 4B parameters ($0.0035/min batch); Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 targets sub-500ms latency ($0.008/min); Voxtral Mini TTS 3 covers 35+ languages and 50+ dialects with emotion and pacing control ($13 per 1M characters). Voice agent API from $0.04/min with Mistral Small 4. Via Mistral's API or self-deployment; comparisons are Mistral's own.

releases.title: Ornith-1.5-122B (open weights, MIT)
releases.summary: A 122B mixture-of-experts reasoning model for coding and agent work that Ornith says serves on a single 80GB GPU; 262,144-token context, extendable to about 1M with YaRN. Lab-reported scores: SWE-bench Verified 84.5, Terminal-Bench 2.1 81.2, SWE-bench Pro 76.9. MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face in BF16 plus FP8, NVFP4, GGUF and MLX builds, and on Ollama (ollama run ornith-1.5:122b). Ornith-1.5 extends Ornith-1.0, which was built on Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4. Benchmarks are Ornith's own.

releases.title: Fibo 2.0 (open weights, image generation + editing)
releases.summary: Bria's 8B-parameter model puts text-to-image and instruction-based image editing in one set of weights, with masked edits and up to 4 reference images, structured JSON (VGL) prompts and better text rendering. Two checkpoints: Fibo 2.0 Dev (full base for fine-tuning) and Edit Turbo (4-step editing). Bria cites #1 among open-weights models for image editing on Artificial Analysis as of Oct 20. Trained only on licensed data; weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (commercial use needs a Bria agreement); also on the Bria API, fal and ComfyUI nodes.

releases.title: FastH3 Omni (open-weight fast video + audio)
releases.summary: FastVideo (Hao AI Lab, UC San Diego) with Nuva Lab open-sourced a distilled MiniMax H3 model for reference-guided video with synchronized stereo audio: a prompt plus up to 9 images, 3 videos and 3 audio clips (12 references max) produces 5–15 second clips at 24 fps in eight transformer evaluations. FastVideo measured up to ~12× lower end-to-end latency than the base model on eight GB200 GPUs; NVFP4 weights and recipes target DGX Spark and RTX 5090, with a ComfyUI FP8 build. Weights use the MiniMax H3 community license.

releases.title: Phonon on-device text-to-speech (open weights)
releases.summary: Tiny streaming TTS models that run offline on phones, laptops, a Raspberry Pi 5 and inside a browser tab: Phonon 31m (English, 64.5 MB, Apache 2.0) and Phonon 40m in English, French, German, Spanish and Portuguese plus a multilingual model (CC BY-NC 4.0, gated). Rust runtime with Python, npm, Swift and Android bindings and an OpenAI-compatible speech server; Gradium says up to 22× faster than real time on an iPhone 16 Pro. Stable runtime v0.4.0 published Oct 20; Gradium's announcement post is dated Oct 21.

releases.title: Ampersand v0.1 (collaborator model)
releases.summary: humans&'s first model is built to help groups of people pursue individual and shared goals over long periods, trained with reinforcement learning on long-horizon social simulations; it can choose to reply or stay silent in a group conversation. Built on GLM 5.3 (about 744B total / 40B active parameters, 1,048,576-token context), text only, API-only via the Agents API as ampersand-v0.1. humans& calls its evaluation results tentative.

releases.title: Beacon: shared memory for coding agents (open source, MIT)
releases.summary: Officially launched Oct 20 alongside a $5.5M seed round: Beacon captures session history across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Cline and 20+ other harnesses into local JSONL, then turns useful workflows, corrections and debugging patterns into reviewed knowledge that future agents retrieve through MCP or Agent Skills. Local-first; MIT-licensed on GitHub (repo public before the launch).

releases.title: Clairic extraction model on Workers AI (preview)
releases.summary: Cloudflare's first System One extraction model (@cf/cloudflare/clairic): send text, plus up to four images, with a schema of typed fields and get one typed value per field (exact text spans with character offsets, numbers, dates, durations, lists, estimates with an 80% interval, and forecasts up to 64 steps), or null when the input doesn't determine it. Every answer carries a confidence score and p_null. Answers in one pass without generating tokens and charges only for input: $0.10 per 1M input tokens; 65,536-token context. Preview on Workers AI; Cloudflare says open weights are coming soon.

releases.title: Mercury 3 (diffusion LLM)
releases.summary: Inception's largest diffusion language model, generating tokens in parallel rather than one at a time: Inception reports 1,068 tokens/s on NVIDIA GPUs and says it matches or beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on its benchmarks while running 4–8× faster. 1M-token context (up from 260K on Mercury 2.5). List price $0.20 / $0.70 per 1M input/output tokens, 50% off at launch ($0.10 / $0.35); cached input 90% off. OpenAI-compatible; on the Inception API, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel, with 100M free tokens for new API keys. Benchmarks are Inception's own.

releases.title: JST-2 (physics-native world model)
releases.summary: Viggle's world foundation model represents scenes as persistent 3D "atoms" instead of pixels. Viggle says it generates an explorable 3D scene (decoded as Gaussian splats) in about one second at under $0.01 of inference, makes animation-ready 3D characters from a single image without separate rigging, and generates full-body motion from text or video. Up to 64 input views as spatial context. Available through Viggle's PINOC app and the Viggle API (100 free credits to start). Comparisons vs Meshy and Tripo are Viggle's own blind tests.

releases.title: TorchNeuron: native PyTorch on Trainium (public beta, Apache 2.0)
releases.summary: An open-source native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium2 and Trainium3: existing PyTorch code runs with a device change ("neuron" instead of "cuda"), with eager mode, torch.compile, native distributed APIs and NKI custom kernels. Announced Oct 19; open-sourced under Apache 2.0 at github.com/aws-neuron/torch-neuronx and in public beta from Oct 20 (Neuron 2.33.0), timed to PyTorch Conference North America.

releases.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
releases.summary: Next-gen Flash model for agentic tasks, coding, computer use and cybersecurity. MiniMax reports ~3× faster online inference and ~70% lower usage cost vs its predecessor; vendor scores include DeepSWE v1.1 73.7%, OSWorld V2 61.7 and CyberGym 82%. Flat API pricing $0.15 / $0.60 / $0.015 per 1M input / output / cached-input tokens; 1M context; multimodal. Was the anonymous Space Bunny Alpha on OpenRouter. Live on the MiniMax API, M Plan and MiniMax Code; open weights promised later (MiniMax says Oct 23). Benchmarks are MiniMax's own.

releases.title: EdenLive real-time generative renderer (open source)
releases.summary: Turns a game engine's rough reference video, a target first frame and a text prompt into detailed or stylized video in real time, while the engine keeps the game logic and world state. 5B and 14B weights plus streaming inference code and a WebRTC real-time service; VAST reports 24+ FPS at 720P, and the 5B model reaches ~24.7 FPS at 1280×704 on one RTX 5090 with LightX2V. Also ships a skill that turns a text prompt into a coarse playable game. Code is Apache 2.0; weights mix licenses and the first-frame workbench component is non-commercial. Release date per secondary coverage (Oct 18); link is the official repo.

releases.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (open weights, MIT) + Search & Fetch APIs
releases.summary: A minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with gains in reasoning, coding, agentic and visual benchmarks (DeepSeek reports DeepSWE v1.1 77.0, up from 74.2; Terminal-Bench 4.0 42.3, up from 31.2) plus shorter outputs and faster task runs. Live on DeepSeek's website, app and API under the same deepseek-flash name at unchanged prices; MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope. DeepSeek also opened its in-house Search & Fetch APIs to everyone at $0.75 per 1,000 calls per endpoint.

releases.title: REA /reverse-engineer skill in Perplexity Computer
releases.summary: Computer can now use REA (Reverse Engineer Anything), morluto's open-source MIT-licensed toolkit, to inspect how an app works without its source code and then build a working version. Tasks that use /reverse-engineer are free through Oct 31, up to 10,000 credits per user. Announced on Perplexity's official Computer account on X.

releases.title: Glimpse (visual thinking model)
releases.summary: Elorian's first model reasons over images and video: tracking objects through motion, reasoning from other viewpoints and predicting physical consequences, with multimodal tools and subagents. Available today via API and Elorian's chat UI at $0.60 / $3.00 per 1M input/output tokens; benchmarks are Elorian's own.

releases.title: RTX Spark laptops go on sale
releases.summary: Windows laptops built on NVIDIA's RTX Spark superchip (Blackwell RTX GPU + Grace CPU) with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI compute, aimed at local AI models and agents, creative apps and gaming. Available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599; pricing varies by region.

releases.title: Cline Cloud sessions (v4.1.25)
releases.summary: Cline can now run a task in a hosted sandbox on a GitHub repo and branch you pick; cloud tasks show in Recent and History, notify you when they finish, and keep running after you close your editor. Rolling out gradually.

releases.title: Beam 1.0 (open weights, Apache 2.0)
releases.summary: Reflection's first open-weight model: a 501B-total / 23B-active MoE with a 1M-token context, built for coding, reasoning and agentic work. Weights in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 on Hugging Face; also on Reflection's API and partners including Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter and OpenCode.

releases.title: Timestral time-series forecasting models (open weights)
releases.summary: Mistral's first time-series foundation models, in 5M, 28M, 123M and 209M sizes, for zero-shot probabilistic forecasts (21 quantiles) over multivariate series with past-only and known-future covariates and up to 32,768 time steps of history. Runs efficiently on CPUs; Mistral says the 209M model ranks first on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench. Weights on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license; code is Apache 2.0.

releases.title: d1-ultra (decision model)
releases.summary: Multimodal decision model that takes text and/or images plus yes/no, choice or score questions and returns calibrated probabilities in one forward pass (no output tokens). Available on the Liquid API at $0.042 per 1M input tokens; Liquid says it leads Artificial Analysis Decision Index by at least 8 points vs other decision models. Aimed at routing, moderation, inspection and agent guardrails rather than chat.

releases.title: SPACE sandbox platform open-sourced (Apache 2.0)
releases.summary: SPACE, the sandbox platform that runs every Perplexity Computer session, is now open source: isolated Firecracker microVMs with pause/resume, snapshots, session branching, and network and credential controls kept outside the sandbox. Akamai, Crusoe and CoreWeave are offering or documenting deployments.

releases.title: FLUX 3 Image Klein (open weights)
releases.summary: A 5.6B-parameter open-weight image model for text-to-image, editing and multi-reference generation (up to 10 reference images), with native 4K output and bounding-box layout control. Weights on Hugging Face under the FLUX Kommunity License; also on the BFL API.

releases.title: Krea 3
releases.summary: Krea's new image-editing model for production work: most edits return in under 8 seconds at native 2K, with characters and products kept consistent across references. Live on krea.ai and via fal, Replicate, OpenRouter, Together AI and others.

releases.title: GPT-Live-1.1 (ChatGPT Voice)
releases.summary: Updated voice model for ChatGPT Voice with more natural accents and new voices in French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Korean and Mexican Spanish. Availability varies by region and account.

releases.title: Muse Spark Open (open weights)
releases.summary: Meta's open-weight multimodal MoE: 816B total / 42B active parameters, 1M-token context, built for coding and agentic work. Weights on Hugging Face; runs locally on M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX, plus vLLM, SGLang and llama.cpp; hosted on OpenRouter, Groq, Together and others.

releases.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt
releases.summary: Open models for agents: Super VL (120B) for servers, Bolt 74B-A9B sized for 24GB local machines with llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio and vLLM support. A 4GB Bolt E4B is due Oct 23.

releases.title: Code Review GA for Claude Team and Enterprise
releases.summary: Automated GitHub pull-request reviews leave research preview; most finish in 6-10 minutes, with Quick, Standard or Deep settings per repo. Eligible Enterprise orgs can claim credits through Jan 15, 2027.

releases.title: Deep Review (public release)
releases.summary: Agentic system that checks technical documents (papers, Docs, slides) for grounded, rigorous feedback. Two free reviews per week; heavier use via your Gemini API key.

releases.title: Gemini 4 Argon
releases.summary: Google's latest frontier model, aimed at hard coding, science and agentic work with a 1M-token limit. Available via API, Antigravity (Ultra), and the Gemini app (Ultra/Pro). Intro price $2/$10 per 1M tokens until Nov 30.

releases.title: Helix World (real-time audio-visual world model, preview)
releases.summary: Start from one image, move with WASD and look with the arrow keys: Helix World, from Noiz AI and HKUST, generates the explorable scene and camera-aligned stereo sound together at 24 fps on a single NVIDIA H800. Try it in the browser at helixworld.org; code (Apache 2.0) and a preview checkpoint are public, and local runs recommend an 80GB GPU. Benchmarks, including the new HelixBench, are Noiz's own.

releases.title: Harness² (open source, Apache 2.0)
releases.summary: Plug-and-play framework for recursively improving an agent's harness (prompts, tools, memory, skills, subagents, scripts, plugins) while keeping model weights fixed. Uses Propose–Probe–Compose without ground-truth verifiers; paper reports gains up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 on JobBench and 11.8 pp on LAB. Code on GitHub under Apache 2.0; paper arXiv:2610.14224.

releases.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
releases.summary: Anthropic's cheapest, fastest small model. Sonnet 5.5 cache reads also halved in price, and Max/Team plans get monthly API credits.

releases.title: GPT-6 with Intelligent UI in ChatGPT
releases.summary: GPT-6 Sol (paid) and Luna (Free/Go) arrive in ChatGPT Chat, answering with interactive UIs. Rollout to paid tiers started Oct 7, Free/Go the next day.

releases.title: dots (cloud-computer agents)
releases.summary: Always-on personal agents rolling out in ChatGPT to Pro and Business Premium users in eligible markets.

releases.title: Claude Opus 5.5
releases.summary: First of the Claude 5.5 family: long-running agentic coding and knowledge work, $4/$20 per 1M tokens, 1M context. Fast mode available in Claude Code.

releases.title: Grok 4.7
releases.summary: Flagship for coding and knowledge work; 500k context, $2/$6 per 1M tokens on the API. Available in Cursor and Grok Build.

releases.title: Agents API (public beta)
releases.summary: Brings the Codex harness and infrastructure to developers via API; pay only for tokens and tools used.

releases.title: Muse personal agent
releases.summary: Meta's personal AI agent for everyday tasks, in a Muse app, WhatsApp and the web. Date per secondary coverage; link is AP News.

releases.title: Projects (beta)
releases.summary: A coordinator agent delegates long-running work to cloud subagents; can subscribe to Slack, PRs and schedules. Exact day not confirmed (September per secondary timeline).
